# Was Next hacked in the supplier data breach?

**Reported.** Reported. Next says outsiders reached some Next data at a supplier, not in Next's own systems, and that no customer data is known affected. No outside party has checked this.

Incident: Was Next hacked? Supplier data breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as Next supplier cyber incident and Next third-party data incident. First published Nov 23, 2026; last updated Nov 23, 2026, 11:13 AM ET.

Picture: A Next store at Treliske Retail Park in Truro, Cornwall, in July 2024. Image: Mutney, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Next,_Treliske_Retail_Park,_Truro,_Cornwall_-_July_2024_(2).jpg).

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 23, 2026, 11:13 AM ET: **Next says a supplier was breached and outsiders reached some Next data; customer data taken is Not established.** New incident page. Sources read: Next's notice to the London Stock Exchange and its investor page (Tier 1); BBC News, The Guardian, Reuters, The Register and City AM, all repeating that one statement. Supplier incident with outsiders reaching Next data: Confirmed by Next's own notice. Next's own systems not compromised: Reported (company's claim). Customer personal data taken: Not established. 'Benign' data: Reported (company's description). Supplier, data types, perpetrator and method: Not established. No ICO or police statement found. Privacy check done: no names, handles or contact details. We opened no leak or dark-web sites.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. No count of affected people applies. Large rests on potential reach, not a measured impact: Next has 800+ stores in the UK and Ireland and sells online, and the supplier is unnamed. Next says no customer personal data is known to be affected. Revisit if more is disclosed.
- Who is affected: Next, whose data a supplier held. Next says no customer personal data is known to be affected; the supplier is unnamed and its other customers are unknown. Be wary of unexpected emails, texts or calls claiming to be from Next, as an outside security firm advised.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|

| Not named | The supplier | Next has not said |

### Known so far

- Next told the stock exchange that a supplier's cyber incident gave outsiders access to certain Next data.

### Not known yet

- Whether any customer personal data was taken.
- Which supplier was hit and what data was accessed.
- Who did it and how. The root cause is not published.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the time of this update on Nov 23, 2026. The root cause has not been published, so this page stays open.

- The name of the supplier, from Next or anyone else.
- A list of what data was accessed, or how much.
- Any statement from the UK data protection regulator (the ICO) or from police. Next does not name the regulator it is working with.
- Any update from Next after its stock-exchange notice.
- Who carried out the incident, how they got in, or any claim of responsibility.

We did not visit any leak, ransomware or dark-web site, forum or channel, and we did not download any data. Everything here comes from Next's own notice and press reports.
